title: Kara:
title_short: Kara · Mom's Day with the Baby Monitor
headline: A working mom checks on her napping baby from her desk, comes home to a stuffy nose, clears it gently with the BN02, and finally gets a quiet minute on the sofa with the baby asleep on the BM04 screen.
story: This is Peter's UGC Video 1: Helping Mom Enjoy a More Reassuring Parenting Experience with BM04 and BN02. No dialogue in the script, so it is music, quick cuts and short on-screen text.

The feeling is relief, not features. Every time the monitor is on screen, the baby is on its screen. The aspirator is used on the nose, gently, on a calm baby. The story ends on the payoff: mom on the sofa, baby asleep, both fine.

Loops: L1 “Is the baby okay while I work?” opens at 0:00 and closes at 0:03 (baby asleep on the screen). L2 “Stuffy nose, what now?” opens at 0:12 and closes at 0:24. Stakes: a working mom who can't be in two places at once.
do: Open mid-glance at the monitor with the hook text already on screen at 0:00.
Hold the baby-on-screen shot 3 to 4 s. The baby must read clearly.
Three BN02 angles, about 3 s each, tip on the nose only.
Fast, casual cuts. Real home, real light.
Mute every clip. Music and small real sounds only.
dont: No logo, no name card, no fade at 0:00.
No monitor shot where the screen does not show the baby.
Never use the case-opening at IMG_9354 00:08 to 00:20, or the box opening in IMG_9355 00:20 to 00:46 (unboxing is banned).
No shot of the baby fussing at the aspirator.
No freeze frames. No Atdhe voice.

bp_intro: Source times are in each clip, read off real keyframes this run (good to about 1 s). The script has no lines, so this cut is music led. All Kara clips are vertical iPhone at about 24 fps. Frames below are real frames from the footage.

rows.frame_alt: Kara at her desk in a purple top, laptop open, the BM04 parent unit on the desk beside her.
rows.visual: IMG_9335.MOV 00:41 to 00:47. She types, glances at the monitor on the desk and picks it up. Start mid-motion on the glance. Do not use 00:00 to 00:30 (the toddler walks in and the camera moves around).
rows.motion: Hook text on frame 1: WFH with a napping baby 🤍 Already on screen at 0:00. Does not animate on. Top third, Inter Bold, white with soft shadow. No logo, no fade.
rows.voice: No voice. Music only. Atdhe is talking behind the camera here: mute the clip sound.
rows.sfx: A soft notification ping as she looks at the monitor.
rows.music: Light, upbeat UGC track starts on frame 1.

rows.frame_alt: Close on the BM04 screen in her hands. The baby is asleep on the screen.
rows.visual: IMG_9335.MOV 00:53 to 00:58. Close on the screen in her hands. Hold 3 to 4 s (the brief asks for it). The baby must read clearly on the screen.
rows.motion: Hook text off on the cut. Small text top third: <q>Baby's asleep. Back to work.</q>

rows.frame_alt: Wide hallway. Kara in a dark jacket walks out the open front door.
rows.visual: IMG_9342.MOV 00:00 to 00:02.5. She walks out the front door. Fast cut. This is the "some time later" beat.

rows.frame_alt: Outside the yellow front door with the red wreath. Kara opens it and walks in.
rows.visual: IMG_9343.MOV 00:03 to 00:08. She opens the yellow door and walks in. Then 1 s of IMG_9341.MOV 00:05 to 00:08: she comes down the stairs with the baby in her arms, smiling.

rows.frame_alt: Kara in a green top on the bed with the baby, making a worried face at the camera.
rows.visual: IMG_9353.MOV 00:40 to 00:50. Playing with the rattle, then she notices and gives the camera a worried look (about 00:47). Use only the last 3 s.
rows.voice: No voice. The clip has Atdhe talking: mute it.

rows.frame_alt: Top-down. Kara cups the baby's head and holds the BN02 tip at the nose, blue light on.
rows.visual: Three angles, about 3 s each (the brief asks for it): IMG_9354.MOV top-down 00:24 to 00:30, then wide side 00:40 to 00:45, then close side 01:04 to 01:10. The tip is on the nose only. Baby is calm in all three. Do not use 00:08 to 00:20 (taking it out of its case).
rows.sfx: Keep a little of the real device sound low under the music.

rows.frame_alt: Kara in lavender loungewear leans over the white crib and lays the baby down.
rows.visual: IMG_9355.MOV 00:05 to 00:12: she holds the baby on her shoulder and soothes her (green top). Then IMG_9350.MOV 00:18 to 00:24: she lays the baby in the crib. This is the only crib shot. She is in the lavender outfit there, which works as "later, in comfy clothes".

rows.frame_alt: Kara on the grey sofa in lavender, a magazine on her lap, the monitor in her hand, smiling.
rows.visual: IMG_9352.MOV 01:10 to 01:24. She reads, checks the monitor and smiles. Do not use 00:34 to 00:48 (her son is on the sofa and the take is broken).

rows.frame_alt: Close on the BM04 screen held in her hands. The baby is clearly asleep on the screen.
rows.visual: IMG_9335.MOV 01:00 to 01:04. Close on the screen. The baby is clearly asleep on it. Use this, not the sofa screen shots in IMG_9352 (00:55 to 01:03), unless you can see the baby on that screen on scrub.
End card: MOMCOZY wordmark in Cozy Chestnut #6A2B3A on Warm Cream #FEF9F6. Product names under it: BM04 Baby Monitor · BN02 Nasal Aspirator.

checklist: Frame 1 is Kara at the desk with the hook text already on screen. No logo, name or fade.
Every monitor shot shows the baby on the screen.
The baby-on-screen shot holds 3 to 4 s.
Three BN02 angles, tip on the nose only, baby calm in all.
No case opening and no box opening anywhere.
No Atdhe voice anywhere. Music and soft real sounds only.
Captions and text in Inter, white with soft shadow, easy to read.
End card is the only logo. MOMCOZY in caps, Cozy Chestnut.

decisions.b: The script says she checks the monitor app on her phone. Kara used the BM04 parent unit instead. The cut uses the parent unit. If Peter needs the app, it was not filmed here.
No visual reference was chosen for this shoot. Atdhe owes it.
The script gives no on-screen text for this video. The lines in the table are ours. Atdhe can change them before V1.

client_note: Why this matters: Peter's rules are strict on this one: real use on the baby, products used correctly, and the baby always on the monitor screen. Their own notes on this brief also ask for real, casual use, not a feature tour.
